main_body: Two-storey timber-frame house: a large tiled hip roof (rows 1-43) over a half-timbered upper wall and a stone-block ground floor with door, windows and a hanging sign
top_band: Roof slope at x=48: tile pattern of brown #8f5c3f with dark #3b232b joints, rows 4-42, under a dark outline at rows 0-3. It is clearly separated from the cream wall below by a dark eave band.
evidence: The roof slope is a large, foreshortened tiled surface visible from above (rows 4-42), with a hip slope on the left and a chimney on top. A dark eave shadow at rows 43-51 sits under the roof edge, and the cream front wall (rows ~49-107) has timber beams and windows with inset dark edges and sills. This matches the roof-over-wall structure of the Beodeul house references, so it reads as a correct 3/4 building.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 4 distinct colours (references: 185 and 66), a median of 3 colours per tile (references: 18 and 11), and 17% flat-fill coverage (references: 0%). The dark edge pixels are 100% neutral, against 7-9% in the references, and the outline reads as a near-black sticker line. The roof tiles are a two-tone brown/dark pattern with no per-tile highlights or intermediate shades. The plaster wall and stone blocks are flat cream with dark joints and no speckle or per-stone shading. This is far thinner than the references.
